correctness.rationale: Every maximum independent set is exactly a size-a clique transversal avoiding joint selection of x and connectors y_i. Necessity follows from pair conflicts and two-vertex blocks; sufficiency constructs transversals for every label pattern using two distinct non-x choices in B0 and two distinct safe choices in every selected large block. The split product polynomial and the sharp a-dimensional VC/Littlestone equality follow. The complex is A glued to a cone x*K along K; K inclusions are nullhomotopic via a fixed non-x B0 vertex. Join/suspension identities yield the stated integral sphere wedges, separate low and high homology dimensions and purity threshold. All quantifiers assume a>=3,n>2a. An independently structured exhaustive Python checker verifies all maximum independent sets, traces, polynomial, adaptive dimension and small-case mod-two Betti ranks for eight test vectors; finite checks are not substituted for the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The 2018 Mohr–Rautenbach theorem determines the unique connected graph maximizing the count of maximum independent sets, but does not identify the Boolean shattered-support complex or its topological transition. The closest exact published published-finding corpus theorem on fully whiskered graphs *does* imply the n=2a boundary, which has been explicitly excluded from new novelty. Its marked modules consist of degree-one private leaves and do not cover n>2a, where nonconnector vertices lie in cliques with mutual edges. Other retrieved results concern maximal rather than maximum independent sets on different graph families. The specific product criterion and pure/nonpure two-tier homotopy classification for F(n,a), n>2a, are not implied by the inspected sources. Novelty is qualified by possible unindexed equivalences.

value.rationale: The connected extremizer F(n,a) is uniquely selected by a nontrivial maximum-independent-set counting theorem, so the concept class is canonical rather than a hand-picked slice. The exact support complex exposes a sharp transition at n=3a from a mixed-dimensional complex with an arbitrarily separated secondary integral homology degree to a pure top-dimensional sphere wedge, while the VC and online dimensions remain a. This connects graph extremality, learning-theoretic traces, and topology and gives all coefficients, facet sizes, and homology ranks for an infinite natural family; novelty does not rest on the already covered whiskered-star boundary.
